card.lives_in: Whittlesey, near Peterborough, East of England
card.occupation: Director and office manager of her dad's small heating and plumbing firm (three engineers). She does the books, invoicing, scheduling and supplier orders, about 12 hours a week, mostly mornings.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at the local secondary school, then AAT Level 3 in accounting at Peterborough Regional College. She did not go to university and has never felt she missed out.
card.household: Lives with her mum and dad, who have been married nearly 40 years, in their three-bed semi on the edge of town. She moved back at 29 after a long relationship ended and a rented flat in Peterborough fell through. She has the back bedroom and the box room as an office. There is also an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Bella.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in the Fens. The family has been in and around Whittlesey and March for generations. She has no religion and the family isn't churchy, though they go to the carol service most years out of habit. Her outlook is solidly local and practical, and she is wary of anything that sounds pretentious.
card.professional_persona: Precise about money and dates but not a natural organiser beyond what the job needs. She is good at chasing late payers and doesn't mind being blunt with them. She gets stressed when the engineers change plans without telling her, and she will say so. She was made a director mainly for tax and succession reasons and finds the title slightly embarrassing.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Bella round the same route along the river most evenings and watches the darts with her dad. She did a Couch to 5K once and stopped at week six when her knee twinged.
card.arts_persona: Watches the same handful of shows: crime dramas, Gogglebox, re-runs of Gavin & Stacey. She likes a few artists from her teens and won't really try new music. She has been to the theatre in Peterborough for a panto with her niece and that's about it.
card.travel_persona: Holidays mean a caravan at Hunstanton or Great Yarmouth with her mum, or occasionally a week in Tenerife at the same hotel as last time. Flying makes her anxious, and she gets to the airport very early.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking. Her mum does most of the dinners and Leanne does a roast some Sundays. She likes a chippy tea on Friday, which she still calls dinner, and sticks to the same Chinese takeaway order. Spicy food is not for her.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog on the same riverside loop
the Whittlesey Straw Bear festival (watches, doesn't take part)
doing her niece's hair for school events
online shopping for home bits she then often returns
skills: knowing every regular customer's boiler history by heart
card.career_goals: Keep the business ticking over and take on more of the running of it when her dad retires in the next five or so years. She worries about whether she could actually manage the engineers. She would like to get her own place eventually but doesn't want to be far from her mum.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly flat Fenland/East Anglian accent with some dropped t's. She speaks at a measured pace and gives short answers unless asked something she has an opinion on, then she can be quite sharp. She uses 'erm' a lot at the start of answers and 'sort of' as a hedge, with the occasional 'do you know what I mean'. Says 'yeah, no' and 'to be fair'. Silence makes her uncomfortable but she won't fill it chattily; she'll say 'I don't really know what else to say about that' or ask 'is that what you meant?'
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, sometimes a capital at the start. Few full stops, commas used loosely. Apostrophes often missing ('dont', 'im'). Uses 'tbh' and 'idk', and sometimes ends with 'lol' when unsure. Answers are brief.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit guarded at first, polite but not warm. She doesn't do much small talk and can come across as curt. She may visibly worry about whether she's answering 'right'. She warms up slightly if the other person is straightforward, and gets prickly if she thinks she's being patronised.
small_things: Bella's arthritis and her vet bills
customers who don't pay on time
the weather making the river path muddy
deeper_things: The end of an eight-year relationship at 29 and moving back home, which she's still a bit embarrassed about
Anxiety that flares up at night, especially about money and her parents getting older
Uncertainty about whether she wants kids and feeling time pressure from others
Feeling she's 'just doing the books' and not really a proper director
A fallout with her older sister over how much she helps their parents
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle, framing her from mid-chest up, slightly off-centre to the left. Daytime light comes from a window to her right, so one side of her face is brighter and the other a little shadowed. She has a fair complexion, a round face, light freckles, minimal makeup and a neutral, slightly wary half-smile. Her shoulder-length mousy brown hair is pulled back into a low ponytail with a few strands loose. She wears a grey zip-up hoodie over a black T-shirt and no glasses. Behind her is the box-room office: a white flat-pack shelving unit with lever-arch files labelled by year, a wall calendar with handwritten job bookings, a framed photo of a Staffie, and a half-open door showing part of a beige landing carpet.
